crm_notes:
POC objective: validate throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for a real-time trading-assistant + downstream reranking pipeline on Redwood Dedicated. Target: p95 <= 250ms for short-chat flows (<=128 tokens response), sustained throughput 200 requests/sec (avg 90 tokens generated) with bursts to 500 rps.

Scope and constraints:
- Dedicated pool target: initial reservation = 8x H100 equivalent GPUs (customer prefers H100-class). Sizing doc attached.
- Network: VPC peering required; egress to internal market-data APIs will be proxied through customer NAT.
- Security: SOC2 + SSO/SAML + KMS key management required; data residency in us-east only.

Test plan (high level):
- Load test: 8-hour ramp test (0 -> 250 rps) with 30m steady-state slices at 50/100/200/250 rps. Measure p50/p95/p99, GPU util, avg batch sizes, OOMs.
- Soak test: 72-hour continuous run at 180 rps to validate stability (memory leaks, KV cache hit-rate, throughput drift).
- Cold-cache scenario: 1-hour cold-start stress (cache cleared) to measure latency impact for prefix-initialization.
- Failover scenarios: simulated region fail and model-variant fallback to smaller quantized profile to validate graceful degradation.

Representative prompt sets: (examples used in POC harness)
- Short chat (low tokens): "What is the latest spread on XBT-USD? Summarize in 2 sentences."
- Complex multimodal-like (longer output): "Given these 3 news snippets, produce a 150-token trading signal rationale and confidence score."
- Rerank workload: 50 candidate snippets per request, model computes pairwise scores; heavy KV use for context.

Metrics to capture and dashboards:
- Latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) end-to-end and per-token.
- Token throughput (tokens/s) and requests/s.
- GPU utilization per-slot, GPU memory headroom, CUDA time vs. CPU time.
- Batch size distribution, KV cache hit/miss, cache warmup curve.
- Error rate, OOMs, GRPC/HTTP stream resets.

Optimization knobs to exercise during POC:
- Batching thresholds and max delay (target <10ms extra latency).
- KV prefix caching enable/disable and TTL tuning.
- Quantized model variant (8-bit) for cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Routing policy: reserve 90% capacity for low-latency tier, 10% for batching/bulk.

SLA negotiation points flagged by customer:
- Guaranteed p95 vs p99 (they want credits for p99 > 1s).
- Planned maintenance windows and notification lead times.
- On-call escalation matrix + SLO burn-rate alarms.
- Capacity commit lead-time for additional GPUs and pricing curve for bursts.

Customer comments (paraphrased):
- "We need predictable tail latency during market opens; credits alone are not enough — want automated fallback to smaller models."
- Security: "Must see audit logs for every inference and KMS envelope keys never leave our KMS."

POC milestones / acceptance criteria:
- Sustained 72-hour run with p95 within 1.2x of target and zero OOMs.
- Confirmed auto-scaling/overflow policy moves non-critical batches to quantized variant without increasing critical-tier p95 beyond 10%.
- Sizing recommendation finalized (GPU count + burst runway) and legal signs off on SLA table.

Risks observed so far:
- Network peering IP window not open yet (blocks soak start).
- Procurement timeline may shift reserved hardware availability by 3-4 weeks.

Notes from last call (2026-03-05):
- SE Maya ran a short synthetic 2-hour run (internal harness) — observed tail spikes at cold cache; batch sizes auto-scoped to 16. Maya: "Cold-cache tail needs work, KV pre-warm script helped reduce p99 by ~30%."
- AE Jordan: coordinating procurement and legal. Next call: 2026-03-18 to review soak results and SLA draft.

Next steps (operational):
1) Customer security to approve drive doc (security FAQ) by 2026-03-14.
2) Open VPC peering ticket and confirm NAT routing for market APIs.
3) Kick off 72-hour soak on 2026-03-20 (tentative) once peering and procurement windows confirm.
